target_customer: Ordinary consumers who wanted to blog and share media without setting up a blog
problem: Blogging was too complicated for most people. Posterous let users publish by sending an email.
business_model: free consumer service with later ad and premium plans, never clearly monetized

founders.name: Sachin Agarwal
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as an Apple engineer; Twitter and Lyft roles came after Posterous.

founders.name: Brett Gibson
founders.background_notes: YC page: wrote software at YC, founded Posterous, Posthaven and Slinkset.

exit.reason: Service closed 2013-04-30 so the team could focus on Twitter

technical_complexity.rationale: Parsing email, handling attachments and auto-posting to other services was straightforward engineering for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Email posting was a copyable feature; Squarespace coverage says Posterous was the only service at launch with it, but rivals like Tumblr could add it.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Tumblr outgrew Posterous per one article; Twitter bought Posterous in March 2012 mostly as an acqui-hire and shut the service 2013-04-30.

market_need_then: Blogging in 2008 required accounts, forms and formatting that put off casual users, while email was universal; Posterous reported more than 15 million monthly users per the YC page.

branding.name_origin: IBTimes reports the name came from Garry Tan shortening the original tagline, the preposterously easy way to blog.

identity.logo: not described by any source found
identity.visual_style: simple, minimal interface matching its dead simple pitch
identity.voice_and_tone: playful and simple (dead simple blogs by email)

branding.brand_signature: The dead simple, blog by email pitch

rebrands.why: Product name after launch of Spaces; reason beyond the new privacy features not sourced.

branding.community_and_virality: Founder interviews and shutdown coverage exist; Posthaven was started by a cofounder as a paid successor after the shutdown.

brand_strength.rationale: Widely covered in tech press and had millions of monthly users at peak, but no evidence of iconic mascot or merch.

outcome_analysis: Posterous grew quickly after the YC Summer 2008 batch, raised a 4.4 million Series A in March 2010 and a 5 million Series B in September 2011, and reported more than 15 million monthly users. Competition from Tumblr and the lack of a clear business model led to a Twitter acqui-hire in March 2012 and a shutdown of the product on April 30, 2013.
notes: Company site returned HTTP 503. Series B 5M from Seedtable and a Spanish government startup database only (aggregators), cross-checked as two outlets but not a press release. CB Insights total 10.14M. Seed 725K in Dec 2008 per Seedtable is unverified. TechCrunch 2010 names Garry Tan as a third founder but the YC page lists only Agarwal and Gibson, so Tan is not listed as a founder here.
